summary.text: Melissa McDonough is a Houston-area realtor and brokerage owner who says she has spent more than 20 years as a volunteer lobbyist in Washington, working on consumer-protection, housing, health care, veterans, and agriculture legislation. She served as an election judge in Harris County and was the 2024 Democratic nominee in this district, losing to Rep. Wesley Hunt. She won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary and describes her message as a "purple solution" built on checks and balances, affordability, and health care.

paragraphs.text: Born in Marietta, Ohio. Her Ballotpedia profile lists her religion as Lutheran.
In a 2024 Ballotpedia survey she described herself as a Tomball resident of 30 years, the wife of a cybersecurity engineer, and the mother of two sons.
Has worked as a realtor and brokerage owner for 30 years, and describes herself as a small business owner.

Says she has spent more than 20 years as a volunteer lobbyist on Capitol Hill, beginning with the National Association of Realtors on behalf of clients denied home loans because of medical debt, and later working with groups including Everytown and the Farm and Ranch Freedom Alliance; she says she has helped champion more than 50 bills.

Says that during the 2022 election she worked as a presiding judge at a Harris County polling site and in ballot board, signature verification, and central count roles, and that she gave witness testimony in lawsuits brought against Harris County over the election.
Has been affiliated with the National Association of REALTORS and the Harris County Democratic Lawyers Association.
Won the March 5, 2024 Democratic primary for the 38th District over Gion Thomas, then lost the November 2024 general election to incumbent Rep. Wesley Hunt, 62.7% to 37.2%.
Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary for the open 38th District seat with 51.6% of the vote, ahead of Marvalette Hunter and Theresa Courts.
